interfaces.purpose: Single rising-edge clock and active-high synchronous reset

signals.name: clk
signals.meaning: All acceptance, completion, and reset changes occur on posedge

signals.name: rst
signals.meaning: Synchronous reset with priority over handshakes

interfaces.purpose: Two independent request sources with active-high hold backpressure

requirements.statement: Source holds request fields stable while req_valid[p] && req_hold[p].
Stimulus uses req_delay from MIN_COMPLETION_DELAY through MAX_COMPLETION_DELAY inclusive.
Stimulus does not present an already-outstanding ID or the same new ID on both sources; accepted violation is reported and DUT behavior is unspecified.
Stimulus does not issue a read without an earlier completed write in the current reset epoch.
Stimulus obeys req_hold[p] only; it must not track, model, or condition on occupancy.
requirements.rationale: No interface-observable signal distinguishes compliant from non-compliant stimulus.

requirements.statement: While rsp_valid && !rsp_ready, response valid and payload fields remain stable until completion or reset.
Every legal completed transaction has status OK; other encodings are reserved and illegal.
Reset overrides request acceptance and response completion.
When req_hold[p] is low at a rising clock edge and req_valid[p] is high, the request on source p is accepted at that edge, unconditionally and independent of the state of the other source.
Accept on a rising edge when req_valid[p] && !req_hold[p].
Complete on a rising edge when rsp_valid && rsp_ready.
req_id is globally unique while outstanding; duplicate avoidance is an environment obligation.
Reuse an ID only after prior completion or reset flush.
Maximum outstanding is 16 and occupancy_next = occupancy + accepted - completed.
Do not accept when acceptance would exceed capacity.
Accept both sources when both valid and at least two slots are free.
Transactions may complete out of acceptance order.
Single response channel completes at most one per cycle; consecutive completions are permitted.
Hold uses beginning-of-edge occupancy; same-edge completion does not free a slot.

When pre-edge occupancy is 15 or more, req_hold[1:0] == 2'b11, including an edge on which a response completes. Depth remains 16; occupancy 16 is a transient cushion slot reachable only in the hold/accept race.
With a free slot and exactly one valid source, accept it.
Accepted edge C with delay D may complete no earlier than C+D, within symbolic bounds.
When multiple transactions are eligible and no response is held, any eligible transaction may be selected.
Write updates associative memory when the write completes.
Read returns latest completed write data at read completion.
Visibility follows completion order, not acceptance order.
Prototype stimulus excludes reads without an earlier completed write in the current epoch.
First reset edge flushes outstanding, clears occupancy, cancels eligibility/watchdog, and advances epoch once.
Pre-reset response is not presented or accepted after reset release.
Flushed IDs may be reused on first operational edge after release.
Synchronous reset is sampled on posedge; reset-only transition and one epoch advance on assertion.
Reset clears DUT associative memory and oracle golden memory.
No handshake on sampled reset edge; while held, holds are high and rsp_valid is low.
Operation resumes on first rising edge with rst low.
Every accepted transaction completes while reset is inactive and response service remains enabled.
Complete within 256 response-service-enabled cycles; reset or rsp_ready low does not advance watchdog.

semantic_decisions.disposition: Pre-edge occupancy controls hold; completion does not free a same-edge slot
Environment obligation; accepted violation is reported and subsequent DUT behavior is unspecified
One clock; active-high synchronous reset dominates handshakes and clears behavioral state; flushed-ID history may persist for classification
A stale-response mutation reserves its flushed ID until the injected response is observed
Per-request eligibility delay is symbolic and bounded; mock defaults are 1 through 8
Legal responses use OK; mock encoding is zero and no DUT error response is modeled
Oracle solely owns semantic state and expected results; scoreboard pairs actual and expected records by observation_seq and reports comparisons

permitted_nondeterminism.permitted_behavior: Any eligible transaction may be selected and completion order/timing remain flexible

observation_fields.meaning: Unique monotonic key for each completed response
Sampled req_hold per source at the rising edge
Sampled req_valid per source at the rising edge
Beginning-of-edge outstanding count for the sampled edge

observations.event: Edge sample: per-source req_hold and req_valid sampled at each rising edge; beginning-of-edge occupancy is the oracle's own book and is never an observed input

oracle_result.purpose: One expected-result record for every completed-response observation, including lifecycle-invalid responses

hold_violation.purpose: One hold-violation record for every INV-016 failure: hold state inconsistent with pre-edge occupancy, or acceptance while hold is low

fields.meaning: Sampled req_hold per source at the rising edge
Beginning-of-edge outstanding count for the sampled edge

state_objects.description: Verification-only completed and flushed ID history

component_ownership.responsibility: Sole owner of lifecycle semantic state, verification-only ID history, expected-result production, and timekeeping from read-only clk/rst/rsp_ready
Buffer and pair actual response and oracle result by observation_seq; compare and report without duplicate semantic state
Publish request accepted observations and protocol facts for both sources
Publish response completion observations with monotonically increasing observation_seq
Publish raw reset transitions and own no epoch or lifecycle state
Own objections, stimulus, drain policy, and zero-outstanding termination guard

checkers.responsibility: Request hold and response stall stability plus reset handshake rules
Expected identity, data, status, and completion-order visibility

assertions.rule: Request fields are stable while req_valid && req_hold
Response fields are stable while rsp_valid && !rsp_ready
Occupancy and acceptance obey capacity and pre-edge rules
No transaction exceeds the response-service-enabled bound

invariants.rule: Every accepted transaction creates exactly one outstanding entry
Every completed response matches one outstanding transaction
Reset removes all outstanding entries and advances epoch
A stale pre-reset response fails after reset deassertion
Read response data follows data requirements
Occupancy equals outstanding table size after every edge
Request fields remain stable while valid and held
Response fields remain stable while valid and not ready
Every legal completed response has OK status
No outstanding transaction exceeds 256 service-enabled cycles
No request or response handshake occurs while reset asserted
Every response observation yields exactly one oracle result and one paired comparison
Hold reflects pre-edge occupancy against the 15 threshold; hold-low implies acceptance

legal_traces.scenario: Two accepted requests complete in reverse order
Both sources accept in one cycle while req_hold is low on both

legal_traces.expected_result: Outstanding and memory state flush; IDs reusable after release

legal_traces.scenario: Minimum and maximum delays become eligible independently and complete out of order
Completed write followed by same-address read
Same-address completion differs from acceptance order
Response stable while ready is low then completes

legal_traces.expected_result: Response completes; request stays held; next occupancy 15

legal_traces.scenario: Exactly one source valid while req_hold[p] is low

generation_gates.condition: Signals and transaction fields have direction, width/model type, producer, and meaning
Every semantic state transition has an observable trigger and state effect
Each component has one responsibility and authoritative state has one owner
Simultaneous-edge behavior is deterministic or explicitly nondeterministic (v0.0e: all simultaneous-edge behavior is deterministic; final-slot arbitration removed with the symmetric-hold rework)
Assumptions, guarantees, mock defaults, and verification-only constraints remain distinct
Every normative requirement maps to observation and checker/invariant/assertion
No blocking semantic-closure decision remains open
Candidate semantic model validates against schema with no unresolved references
Later generation manifest records mock parameters, encodings, source, and generator revision
